news.headline: TSA Bans Sitting Down for Airport ID Checkers, Because Standing Makes You More Alert (Apparently)
news.summary: 米運輸保安局（TSA）が、空港の保安検査場でIDや搭乗券を確認する係員に対し、業務中の着席を禁止すると発表した。TSAは「警戒心の維持」を理由に挙げているが、職員組合は安全性と「基本的な礼節」を無視した措置だと批判している。

commentary: 矛盾: 「立ってれば頭が働く」という理屈、お医者さんに聞いたんですかね。長時間立ちっぱなしの人間がより注意力を発揮するというエビデンス、見てみたいんですよ。
滑稽さ: 偽造IDを見破るために必要なのが「椅子を取り上げること」だったとは。何年もそれを見逃してたのは、座ってたせいだったんですか。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本の役所で「立ち続けなさい、そのほうが仕事がはかどる」なんて通達が出たら即ニュースになりますよね。アメリカでは「警戒心」という言葉が万能の魔法として使われるのが、端から見るとなかなか。
imagePrompts: A TSA checkpoint where the ID-checking podium has an empty chair behind it, a chain and padlock wrapped around it, and a handwritten 'OUT OF SERVICE' sign taped to the seat. A government memo is pinned to the podium.

A conference room inside TSA headquarters: a whiteboard reads 'ALERT LEVELS' with a diagram showing a seated figure labeled 'DANGER' and a standing figure labeled 'VIGILANCE.' Empty coffee cups everywhere.
A long airport security hallway, ID-checking officers standing rigidly at their podiums, legs visibly tired, while a massive framed poster behind them reads 'STAYING ALERT KEEPS AMERICA SAFE.'
captions: TSA found the secret to airport security: it was chairs. Chairs were the problem the whole time.
The union called it a violation of 'common decency.' The TSA called it 'alertness.' Somewhere between those two is a very tired person checking your Delta boarding pass.
Eight hours on your feet, staring at boarding passes — because the lower back is where false IDs hide.
They've spent years failing to catch fake IDs, but finally: a culprit. It was the chair.
Other agencies got body cameras. These guys lost a chair.
captionsJa: 空港セキュリティの盲点、ついに発見。椅子でした。ずっと椅子のせいだったんです。
組合は「基本的な礼節の侵害」と言い、TSAは「警戒心の向上」と言う。その間で、あなたの搭乗券を確認してるのは腰が限界の人間ですよ。
8時間立ちっぱなし。偽造IDは腰痛の向こうに隠れているから。
何年も偽造IDを見逃してきた。でも犯人はわかった。椅子です。
他の機関はボディカメラを導入した。この人たちは椅子を没収された。
candidates.newsEn: The Transportation Security Administration has announced a new rule banning airport ID-checking officers from sitting while verifying passengers' boarding passes and IDs at security checkpoints. The TSA says the change is designed to keep officers more alert on the job. The union representing these workers pushed back, saying the rule ignores both physical safety concerns and basic human dignity.

ironyEn.contradiction: The TSA's whole job is to catch threats — and apparently the biggest threat they identified was a chair.
ironyEn.absurdity: Years of missed fake IDs, smuggled liquids, and the occasional forgotten firearm, and the fix was: stand up.
ironyEn.outside: Most countries issue standing desks as ergonomic improvements. America issues them as punishment disguised as policy.

ironyEn.contradiction: They want officers more alert, but there's actual research showing prolonged standing increases fatigue and reduces cognitive performance.
ironyEn.absurdity: The security theater just added a new act — now the performers have to do it on their feet.
ironyEn.outside: Unionized workers in most of the developed world fight to get sit-stand desks. These workers are fighting just to get the 'sit' part back.

news.headline: Tesla's Driverless Taxi Had a Rocky First Month in Austin — Now It Wants to Go Everywhere
news.summary: テスラの自律走行ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」はオースティンで運行を開始してから約1ヶ月が経過したが、出だしは順調とは言い難い状況にある。それでも同社は今後の全国展開を視野に入れており、サイバーキャブの成功がテスラの自動車販売依存からの脱却を左右するとされている。

commentary: 矛盾: 「自動運転で人間を超える」と言ってた会社が、最初の1ヶ月でつまずいた。でも次の街に行きます、というのは、ちょっと自動運転の比喩として出来すぎてる。
滑稽さ: テスラの未来はサイバーキャブにかかってる。そのサイバーキャブの最初の1ヶ月が「rocky（岩だらけ）」。走行記録かと思ったら会社の状況の話でした。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本では自動運転の実証実験に何年もかけて、それでも慎重に進める。「1ヶ月でうまくいかなかったけど次の都市へ」という速度感は、シリコンバレー以外の感覚では「え、もう？」以外の言葉が出てこない。
imagePrompts: A sleek futuristic driverless taxi parked at a slightly odd angle on an Austin street, a traffic cone tipped over nearby, a small crowd of confused onlookers, and a 'COMING SOON TO YOUR CITY' banner zip-tied to a lamppost above it.
A Tesla boardroom presentation slide that reads 'Month 1: Rocky.' followed by a slide that reads 'Month 2: Everywhere.' with a map of the entire United States covered in blinking dots.
A Cybercab robotaxi at a stoplight, a GPS screen inside showing a spinning loading wheel, with a speech bubble from the empty driver seat reading 'Recalculating...'
captions: Month one: rocky. Month two: your city. Tesla skips the 'fix it' part.
The whole company's future rides on this taxi — and the taxi is still figuring out Austin.
No driver means no one to fire when it goes wrong. Honestly, that might be the real innovation.
They've been promising full self-driving since 2016. Austin's just the latest beta test that graduated early.
Rocky first month in one city. Solution? More cities. This is either genius or the plot of a disaster movie.
captionsJa: 1ヶ月目は散々。2ヶ月目は全国展開。「修正する」という工程、どこ行ったんですか。
会社の未来を背負ったタクシーが、オースティンをまだ理解しきれてない。
ドライバーがいないから、何かあっても誰もクビにできない。これが本当のイノベーションかもしれない。
2016年から「もうすぐ完全自動運転」と言い続けてきた。オースティンはその最新ベータ版です。
1都市で1ヶ月うまくいかなかった。解決策は「もっと都市を増やす」。天才か、パニック映画か。
candidates.newsEn: Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi launched in Austin about a month ago as a cornerstone of Elon Musk's plan to move the company beyond traditional car sales. The first month has been described as rocky, with various operational challenges emerging. Despite the difficult start, Tesla is now planning to expand the service to additional cities, raising questions about whether the problems from month one are truly resolved.

ironyEn.contradiction: Tesla says the future of the company depends on Cybercab working — and the first month didn't work great — so naturally, the move is to expand.
ironyEn.absurdity: Nothing fixes a rocky launch like taking it to a brand new city where there are even more things to go wrong.
ironyEn.outside: Most companies debug before scaling. Tesla apparently debugs by scaling.

ironyEn.contradiction: Musk has been promising full self-driving 'next year' for about a decade. Austin was supposed to be the proof. The proof needs more proof.
ironyEn.absurdity: The Cybercab is driverless, which means when it gets lost, there's no one to blame. That's actually the most Silicon Valley thing ever designed.
ironyEn.outside: Toyota spent years on safety certification before launching any autonomous pilot. Tesla spent a month and declared it time to expand. Different philosophies, same roads.

news.headline: Trump Pushes Daylight Saving Time Bill by Sharing What Appears to Be a Senator's Personal Cell Number
news.summary: トランプ大統領は、サマータイムを恒久化する法案を支持するよう、アーカンソー州選出の共和党上院議員トム・コットンに圧力をかけ、コットン氏の個人的な電話番号とみられる番号をSNSで一般公開した。

commentary: 矛盾: 大統領が自党の上院議員に「国民、電話してやって」と頼む。政党内の説得ってそういうやり方でしたっけ。ホワイトハウスの直通電話、つながらなかったのかな。
滑稽さ: サマータイムを永久にするために、上院議員の個人番号っぽい番号を全国にばらまく。政策ロビー活動の歴史の中でも、かなり独自の手法だと思います。
日本・海外から見ると: 日本で首相が「この大臣の携帯に電話してください」とSNSに投稿したら、翌日には辞任会見ですよ。アメリカでは「戦略」として報道されるのが面白い。
imagePrompts: A large social media post screenshot framed like a presidential proclamation, with a phone number prominently displayed, and tiny illustrated people holding phones flooding toward it like ants toward sugar.

A senator's desk overwhelmed with ringing phones stacked on top of each other, each one vibrating off the edge, as a clock on the wall reads both 2:00 and 3:00 simultaneously with question marks between them.
The White House briefing room podium with a giant poster that reads 'CALL TOM' and an oversized phone number, podium labeled with a small plaque: 'Official Policy Communication.'
captions: Can't convince your own senator? Post his number to 80 million people. The whip system had a good run.
Daylight saving time: the issue so urgent it required doxxing a Republican.
Tom Cotton's phone is ringing. It's America. All of it.
This is either governing or a prank call campaign. Possibly both.
The president wants to save daylight — starting with whatever's left of Tom Cotton's afternoon.
captionsJa: 自党の上院議員を説得できない？ 8000万人に番号を投げればいい。党内の根回しって、そういうことでしたっけ。
サマータイム恒久化。そのために共和党議員をドックスする必要があった。
トム・コットンの電話が鳴ってる。アメリカから。全員から。
これは政治なのか、いたずら電話キャンペーンなのか。たぶん両方。
大統領は昼の時間を守りたい。まずトム・コットンの午後を犠牲にして。
candidates.newsEn: President Trump took to social media Saturday to pressure Republican Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas into supporting legislation that would make daylight saving time permanent. In doing so, Trump appeared to share what may be Cotton's personal phone number, urging Americans to call him directly. The move came as part of Trump's push for a clock-change policy that has seen renewed interest in Congress.

ironyEn.contradiction: The president of the United States, unable to persuade a member of his own party through normal channels, outsourced the lobbying to the general public.
ironyEn.absurdity: American democracy: where a senator's phone number goes viral because the guy with the nuclear codes needed backup.
ironyEn.outside: Most governments have internal whipping mechanisms for this. The US now has a social media post and an apparently very busy phone line.

ironyEn.contradiction: Trump wants to end the twice-yearly disruption of changing clocks — and chose to do it by creating a different kind of disruption: flooding a senator's phone.
ironyEn.absurdity: Cotton's personal cell, potentially shared with every American who follows Trump online, as a policy tool. The senator's contact list just got a lot longer.
ironyEn.outside: In parliamentary systems, party leaders use the whip. Trump uses the share button. Both are forms of pressure, but only one involves your phone ringing at 2 AM from strangers in Idaho.

news.headline: OpenAI Safety Employee Quits, Publishes Warning — As OpenAI Releases More AI
news.summary: OpenAIで主要モデルのリリースごとに安全性レポートを執筆していたデイビッド・ロビンソン氏が同社を退職し、AIの安全性への懸念を公開書簡で表明した。同氏は雑誌「ジ・アトランティック」への寄稿で警鐘を鳴らしており、OpenAIでは安全担当者の退職が相次いでいる。

commentary: 矛盾: OpenAIの「安全レポート」を書いていた人が、安全ではないと感じて辞める。会社のブレーキを作ってた人がブレーキをかけて去っていく構図、わかりやすすぎて笑えない。
滑稽さ: 「AIは安全です」というレポートを書いてた人が「実は安全じゃないかも」と言いながら辞める。そのレポート、誰が書くんですか、これから。
日本・海外から見ると: 原子力発電所の安全基準を書いてた担当者が「やばいと思う」と言って辞めたら大ニュースですよ。テック業界だとなぜか「またか」で済んでしまうのが、海外から見ると不思議でしかない。
imagePrompts: A large corporate office desk covered in stacked safety reports labeled 'MODEL X: SAFE,' 'MODEL Y: SAFE,' 'MODEL Z: SAFE,' with a resignation letter on top that reads simply 'I don't think so.' A cardboard box of personal items sits on the floor nearby.

A revolving door at OpenAI headquarters with a steady stream of people in 'SAFETY TEAM' lanyards walking out, each carrying a laptop and a manila envelope, as a banner above the entrance reads 'Safety First.'
A split image: on the left, a framed OpenAI safety certificate on a wall; on the right, the same certificate in a recycling bin next to a printed-out Atlantic op-ed.
captions: The man who wrote 'this AI is safe' quit to write 'actually, about that.'
OpenAI's safety reports: authored by someone who no longer trusts OpenAI's safety. Details at 11.
He wrote the green lights. He left through the red one.
Another month, another OpenAI safety staffer with a magazine deal and a lot to say.
The company that put 'safe' in its founding documents keeps losing the people who were supposed to check.
captionsJa: 「このAIは安全です」と書いてた人が「やっぱりそうじゃないかも」と書いて辞めた。
OpenAIの安全レポート。書いた本人がOpenAIを信頼していない。詳細は続報で。
青信号を書いてた人が、赤信号で去っていった。
また今月もOpenAIの安全担当者が雑誌に寄稿しながら辞めた。
「安全」を社名に掲げた会社が、安全を確認する人を次々と失っている。
candidates.newsEn: David Robinson, an OpenAI safety employee responsible for writing safety reports accompanying every major model release, resigned this week and published an editorial in The Atlantic raising alarms about the company's direction. Robinson is among a series of safety-focused employees to leave OpenAI in recent months. The company continues to develop and release new AI models.

ironyEn.contradiction: The person whose job was to certify that OpenAI's models were safe enough to release has decided that OpenAI is not safe enough to stay at.
ironyEn.absurdity: Every safety report he wrote was a green light. His resignation letter is the red one.
ironyEn.outside: If the chief safety inspector at a nuclear plant quit and wrote an op-ed, we'd probably pause. We apparently don't apply that logic to AI.

ironyEn.contradiction: OpenAI was founded specifically with safety as its core mission. The guy writing the safety documents no longer feels safe writing them.
ironyEn.absurdity: He's the author of the reassurances. He's unpersuaded by his own body of work. That's a new genre of whistleblowing.
ironyEn.outside: Readers outside the US keep watching ex-OpenAI safety staffers publish warnings at a pace that now has its own publication pattern: quit, write Atlantic piece, repeat.

news.headline: Pentagon Gets an 'Office of Religious Affairs' Under Hegseth, Who Famously Dislikes 'Weirdos'
news.summary: ピート・ヘグセス国防長官が国防総省に「宗教問題局」を新設すると発表した。ヘグセス長官は「あごひげを生やした者、変人、弱虫は不要」などの発言で知られており、今回の動きは国防総省のキャラクターに関する議論を呼んでいる。

commentary: 矛盾: 「変人と弱虫はいらない」と言ってた国防長官が、ペンタゴンに「宗教局」を作る。軍の強さとは何か、という問いへの答えがだいぶ独特な方向に向かってるんですよ。
滑稽さ: 「ビアード（あごひげ）はダメ」と言ってる人が宗教局を作る。宗教の歴史の中で、あごひげがどれだけ神聖視されてきたか、少し調べてみてほしい。
日本・海外から見ると: 政教分離が憲法の原則のはずのアメリカで、国防総省が宗教局を設置する。「国の防衛」と「宗教行政」が同じ省庁で机を並べる光景、なかなかのものですよ。
imagePrompts: A Pentagon corridor with a brand new frosted glass door labeled 'OFFICE OF RELIGIOUS AFFAIRS,' next to an older door with a 'NO BEARDOS' sign still taped to it. The hallway is empty except for a visitor badge lying on the floor.

An organizational chart of the Pentagon with a newly added box at the bottom reading 'Office of Religious Affairs' connected by a dotted line to the Secretary of Defense office, surrounded by question marks from neighboring departments.

A formal government plaque being mounted on a Pentagon wall that reads 'Office of Religious Affairs — Est. 2026,' while in the reflection of the polished plaque, a framed copy of the First Amendment is visible on the wall behind.
captions: No room for weirdos. Plenty of room for a whole new religious bureaucracy.
He banned beards. He opened a religion office. These two facts are about to have a very awkward meeting.
The Pentagon: officially tough on wimps, soft on theocracy.
When you said you wanted a stronger military, this might not be what you pictured.
Other defense departments have acquisition offices. Ours now has one for the afterlife.
captionsJa: 変人はお断り。宗教を扱う局は大歓迎。
あごひげを禁止した人が宗教局を作った。この二つの事実、いずれ正面衝突しますよ。
ペンタゴン：弱虫には厳しく、神政政治には優しい。
「強い軍」を求めていた人たち、これが求めてたものでしたか？
他国の国防省には調達局がある。アメリカには今、来世担当局がある。
candidates.newsEn: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has announced the creation of a new Office of Religious Affairs at the Pentagon. Hegseth, who has publicly declared that the military has no room for 'beardos, weirdos and wimps,' is now adding a dedicated religious office to the Defense Department's organizational chart. The move is part of a broader reshaping of Pentagon priorities under the current administration.

ironyEn.contradiction: The man who declared the military must purge 'weirdos' is now building an office dedicated to the spiritual dimension of warfare. The Pentagon apparently has room for God but not eccentricity.
ironyEn.absurdity: He's anti-beard, which means he's already theologically opposed to roughly half of recorded religious history.
ironyEn.outside: The First Amendment separates church from state. Hegseth is separating beards from service while uniting church and Defense Department. Constitutional scholars are having a week.

ironyEn.contradiction: The Office of Religious Affairs is being set up inside the world's largest military bureaucracy, by a secretary who has made toughness his entire brand.
ironyEn.absurdity: Turns out 'beardos, weirdos and wimps' was the shortlist of people unwelcome — but if you bring a Bible, you've got a whole department now.
ironyEn.outside: Most NATO allies are actively trying to keep religion out of military command structures. The US just gave it a nameplate.

editorial.thread: 今日の5本を貫く糸は「見張り番が消えていく」こと。TSAの係員は立たされ、テスラは転んで次の街へ、OpenAIの安全担当者は辞表を出し、トランプは味方の電話番号をばらまき、ペンタゴンに宗教局ができる。誰かが何かを守ろうとするたびに、守り方がどんどん変になっていく。
editorial.titleEn: Nobody's Minding the Store (But They're Standing Up Straight)
editorial.subtitleEn: Five stories about who's supposed to be watching — and what they're doing instead.
editorial.titleJa: OpenAIの「安全レポート」を書いていた人が、安全じゃないと言って辞めた話
titleAltJa: 今日のアメリカ：椅子を取り上げたら安全になる、という理論が国家機関から出てきた
「誰が見張ってんの?」って5回言いたくなるニュースが今日4本と、笑えない1本あります
editorial.leadJa:
TSAが椅子を禁止しました。テスラが転んだまま次の街に向かいます。OpenAIの安全担当者が辞めながら「やばい」と言い残していきました。

見張り番が、ちょっとずつおかしくなってる。今日はそういう日です。
editorial.introEn:
Five people — or institutions — whose job it is to keep things safe, stable, or at least pointed in the right direction. And today, every single one of them is doing something else entirely.

TSA pulled the chairs from the people checking your ID at the airport. Tesla's robotaxi had a rough first month in Austin and is now heading to your city. OpenAI's safety guy quit and wrote an op-ed on the way out. Trump apparently texted a senator's personal number to eighty million followers. And the Pentagon got a religion office from the guy who said 'no weirdos.'

Here's your forecast: if you've been quietly holding things together at work while the people above you make increasingly strange decisions, today's news says you're not imagining it. That counts for something. Probably won't get you a raise, but it counts.
editorial.introJa:
TSA（アメリカの空港保安局）が椅子を撤去しました。

IDをチェックする係員の椅子を。「立っていたほうが頭が働く」という理由で。

この一文を読んで、私は少し遠くを見ました。

で、他を見ると…テスラのロボタクシーが最初の1ヶ月で転びながら次の街に向かい、OpenAIの安全担当者が「やばいと思う」と書いて辞め、トランプ大統領が自党の上院議員の個人電話番号をSNSにばらまき、ペンタゴンに「宗教局」ができています。

今日を貫く糸は、たぶん「見張り番が迷子」ということです。安全を守るはずの人たちが、守り方を見失ってる。

ということで、占いです。あなたが「なんで私がちゃんとしなきゃいけないんだろう」と思っていることがあるなら、今日のニュースはその答えです。上がそういう状態だから、下がしっかりするしかない。不公平だけど、今日のあなたの「ちゃんと」は、ちゃんと意味があります。少なくとも今日はね。
editorial.quipEn: Turns out the hardest job in America is being the person responsible for safety at any institution that has the word 'safety' in the job title.
editorial.quipJa: 「安全担当者」という肩書の人が次々に辞めていく職場、ちょっと待って、それどこの話ですかって聞いたら、全部違う会社でした。
notesEn: TSA has banned ID-checkers from sitting at airport security. The reason: standing keeps you more alert. The union's response: this ignores physical safety and basic dignity. Eight hours on your feet, staring at Delta boarding passes — because apparently that's what stands between us and chaos.
Tesla's Cybercab had a rough first month in Austin. Tesla's response: expand to more cities. There's something almost admirable about skipping the 'fix it' step entirely.

Trump wanted a senator to vote for his daylight saving bill. His approach: post what looks like the senator's personal cell number to 80 million followers. Most persuasive use of social media in a legislative context, I'll give him that.

The man who wrote OpenAI's safety reports for every major model release quit this week. On the way out, he published a piece in The Atlantic raising alarms about where the company is headed. Someone still has to write those reports. That person will presumably be more optimistic about the situation.

Pete Hegseth, who said the military has no room for 'beardos, weirdos and wimps,' has created a new Office of Religious Affairs at the Pentagon. The irony involving beards and religious history is available to anyone who wants it.
xJa: アメリカの空港保安係員が「椅子禁止」になりました。理由は「立ってると頭が働く」。8時間立ちっぱなしの人間が最も鋭い、という研究、見てみたいな。
テスラのロボタクシー、最初の1ヶ月は「rocky（順調とは言い難い）」。次の一手は「別の街に展開」。「直す」という選択肢、なかったんですかね。
トランプ大統領、サマータイム法案のために自党の上院議員の個人番号っぽいものをSNSで公開しました。8000万人に「電話して」。党内の話です、これ。
OpenAIの「安全レポート」を書いていた担当者が退職し、「実は心配しています」という記事を書きました。次のレポート、誰が書くんだろう。
「変人と弱虫は軍に不要」と言ったヘグセス国防長官がペンタゴンに「宗教問題局」を新設。あごひげと宗教の歴史的関係、調べてから発表してほしかった。
raidEn: Standing for eight hours makes you more alert, according to people who have not stood for eight hours.
Rocky first month, expansion plan confirmed — Tesla really did build a self-driving company in the most self-driving way possible.
Tom Cotton's phone is ringing. It's America. All of it.
He wrote 'this model is safe.' Then he left to write 'about that, actually.' The sequel is always darker.
He banned beards. He opened a religion office. History has a sense of humor even when the people making it don't.
raidJa: 「立つと警戒心が高まる」という理論、職員の腰には一ミリも触れていないんですよね。よく読んだ記事でした。
最初の1ヶ月が順調じゃなかったのに次の街へ、という判断の速さ、シリコンバレー以外の感覚では「え、もう?」しか出てこないですよね。面白い記事でした。
「電話して」と言って議員の番号を公開する。これが2026年のロビー活動なんですね。よく読んだ記事でした。

editorial.fullEn:
# Nobody's Minding the Store (But They're Standing Up Straight)

## Today's Forecast

Five people — or institutions — whose job it is to keep things safe, stable, or at least pointed in the right direction. And today, every single one of them is doing something else entirely.

TSA pulled the chairs from the people checking your ID at the airport. Tesla's robotaxi had a rough first month in Austin and is now heading to your city. OpenAI's safety guy quit and wrote an op-ed on the way out. Trump apparently texted a senator's personal number to eighty million followers. And the Pentagon got a religion office from the guy who said 'no weirdos.'

Here's your forecast: if you've been quietly holding things together at work while the people above you make increasingly strange decisions, today's news says you're not imagining it. That counts for something. Probably won't get you a raise, but it counts.

---

## 1. TSA Bans Sitting Down for Airport ID Checkers, Because Standing Makes You More Alert (Apparently)

*The Guardian US — [source](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/03/tsa-rule-change)*

The Transportation Security Administration has announced a new rule banning airport ID-checking officers from sitting while verifying passengers' boarding passes and IDs at security checkpoints. The TSA says the change is designed to keep officers more alert on the job. The union representing these workers pushed back, saying the rule ignores both physical safety concerns and basic human dignity.

**Why It's Funny**

TSA's new rule: no sitting for ID-checkers at security. The reasoning is that standing keeps officers more alert. I'd love to see the study. Because every doctor, physical therapist, and person who has worked a retail shift knows that eight hours on your feet does something to your attention — and 'sharp and focused' isn't the word they'd choose. The union called it a dignity issue. TSA called it a security upgrade. Somewhere between those two positions is a very sore human being staring at your boarding pass, heroically upright, catching nothing.

**Say It Out Loud**

> TSA found the secret to airport security: it was chairs. Chairs were the problem the whole time.

---

## 2. Tesla's Driverless Taxi Had a Rocky First Month in Austin — Now It Wants to Go Everywhere

*CNBC Top News — [source](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/03/tesla-cybercab-pressure-to-expand-after-rocky-first-month-in-austin.html)*

Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi launched in Austin about a month ago as a cornerstone of Elon Musk's plan to move the company beyond traditional car sales. The first month has been described as rocky, with various operational challenges emerging. Despite the difficult start, Tesla is now planning to expand the service to additional cities, raising questions about whether the problems from month one are truly resolved.

**Why It's Funny**

The Cybercab launched in Austin. Month one: rocky. Month two: expansion to new cities. Tesla has essentially applied the 'move fast' philosophy to a product whose entire value proposition is that it does not move fast recklessly. The whole company's future is riding on this taxi. The taxi is still figuring out Austin. These two facts are in the same press release.

**Say It Out Loud**

> Month one: rocky. Month two: your city. Tesla skips the 'fix it' part.

---

## 3. Trump Pushes Daylight Saving Time Bill by Sharing What Appears to Be a Senator's Personal Cell Number

*The Guardian US — [source](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/03/trump-tom-cotton-daylight-saving-time)*

President Trump took to social media Saturday to pressure Republican Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas into supporting legislation that would make daylight saving time permanent. In doing so, Trump appeared to share what may be Cotton's personal phone number, urging Americans to call him directly. The move came as part of Trump's push for a clock-change policy that has seen renewed interest in Congress.

**Why It's Funny**

Trump wanted Senator Tom Cotton to vote for permanent daylight saving time. Cotton wasn't convinced. So Trump posted what appears to be Cotton's personal cell number and asked eighty million people to call him directly. This is a sitting president lobbying his own party's senator through crowd-sourced harassment. The bill is about clocks. The method rewound something else entirely.

**Say It Out Loud**

> Can't convince your own senator? Post his number to 80 million people. The whip system had a good run.

---

## 4. OpenAI Safety Employee Quits, Publishes Warning — As OpenAI Releases More AI

*The Verge — [source](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1004408/openai-safety-quits-sounding-the-alarm)*

David Robinson, an OpenAI safety employee responsible for writing safety reports accompanying every major model release, resigned this week and published an editorial in The Atlantic raising alarms about the company's direction. Robinson is among a series of safety-focused employees to leave OpenAI in recent months. The company continues to develop and release new AI models.

**Why It's Funny**

David Robinson wrote the safety reports that went out with every major OpenAI model release. Every time the company said 'this is safe,' his name was on it. This week he resigned and published a piece in The Atlantic saying he has concerns about where OpenAI is headed. Someone will write the next safety report. That person will, by definition, be someone who hasn't quit yet.

**Say It Out Loud**

> The man who wrote 'this AI is safe' quit to write 'actually, about that.'

---

## 5. Pentagon Gets an 'Office of Religious Affairs' Under Hegseth, Who Famously Dislikes 'Weirdos'

*The Guardian US — [source](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/oct/03/pete-hegseth-office-of-religious-affairs)*

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has announced the creation of a new Office of Religious Affairs at the Pentagon. Hegseth, who has publicly declared that the military has no room for 'beardos, weirdos and wimps,' is now adding a dedicated religious office to the Defense Department's organizational chart. The move is part of a broader reshaping of Pentagon priorities under the current administration.

**Why It's Funny**

Pete Hegseth, who announced that the military has no place for 'beardos, weirdos and wimps,' has created a new Office of Religious Affairs inside the Pentagon. Religious tradition and facial hair have a long, well-documented relationship. Hegseth is now officially in charge of both. The Pentagon's org chart has seen stranger things, probably. Actually, I'm not sure it has.

**Say It Out Loud**

> No room for weirdos. Plenty of room for a whole new religious bureaucracy.

---

## Today's Punchline

> Turns out the hardest job in America is being the person responsible for safety at any institution that has the word 'safety' in the job title.
editorial.fullJa:
# OpenAIの「安全レポート」を書いていた人が、安全じゃないと言って辞めた話

## 今日を占うよ〜

TSA（アメリカの空港保安局）が椅子を撤去しました。

IDをチェックする係員の椅子を。「立っていたほうが頭が働く」という理由で。

この一文を読んで、私は少し遠くを見ました。

で、他を見ると…テスラのロボタクシーが最初の1ヶ月で転びながら次の街に向かい、OpenAIの安全担当者が「やばいと思う」と書いて辞め、トランプ大統領が自党の上院議員の個人電話番号をSNSにばらまき、ペンタゴンに「宗教局」ができています。

今日を貫く糸は、たぶん「見張り番が迷子」ということです。安全を守るはずの人たちが、守り方を見失ってる。

ということで、占いです。あなたが「なんで私がちゃんとしなきゃいけないんだろう」と思っていることがあるなら、今日のニュースはその答えです。上がそういう状態だから、下がしっかりするしかない。不公平だけど、今日のあなたの「ちゃんと」は、ちゃんと意味があります。少なくとも今日はね。

---

## 1. TSA Bans Sitting Down for Airport ID Checkers, Because Standing Makes You More Alert (Apparently)

*The Guardian US（[記事](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/03/tsa-rule-change)）*

米運輸保安局（TSA）が、空港の保安検査場でIDや搭乗券を確認する係員に対し、業務中の着席を禁止すると発表した。TSAは「警戒心の維持」を理由に挙げているが、職員組合は安全性と「基本的な礼節」を無視した措置だと批判している。

**どこが笑える？**

TSAが「係員は座ってはいけない」というルールを出しました。理由は「立っているほうが警戒心が高まる」。8時間立ちっぱなしで迎える午後3時の頭の状態、医者に聞きましたか。職員組合は「安全性と礼節の両方を無視している」と反発しています。偽造IDを見破るために必要だったのが「椅子を取り上げること」だったとは。何年も座りながら見逃してきたのだとしたら、それはそれで別の問題だと思うんですが。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 空港セキュリティの盲点、ついに発見。椅子でした。ずっと椅子のせいだったんです。

---

## 2. Tesla's Driverless Taxi Had a Rocky First Month in Austin — Now It Wants to Go Everywhere

*CNBC Top News（[記事](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/03/tesla-cybercab-pressure-to-expand-after-rocky-first-month-in-austin.html)）*

テスラの自律走行ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」はオースティンで運行を開始してから約1ヶ月が経過したが、出だしは順調とは言い難い状況にある。それでも同社は今後の全国展開を視野に入れており、サイバーキャブの成功がテスラの自動車販売依存からの脱却を左右するとされている。

**どこが笑える？**

テスラのサイバーキャブ、オースティンでの最初の1ヶ月は「rocky（険しかった）」と報じられています。次の手は「他の都市への展開」。「修正する」という選択肢、検討したんですかね。テスラの未来はこのタクシーにかかっているらしい。そのタクシーがまだオースティンで迷っている。この2つが同じ発表の中に並んでいます。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 1ヶ月目は散々。2ヶ月目は全国展開。「修正する」という工程、どこ行ったんですか。

---

## 3. Trump Pushes Daylight Saving Time Bill by Sharing What Appears to Be a Senator's Personal Cell Number

*The Guardian US（[記事](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/03/trump-tom-cotton-daylight-saving-time)）*

トランプ大統領は、サマータイムを恒久化する法案を支持するよう、アーカンソー州選出の共和党上院議員トム・コットンに圧力をかけ、コットン氏の個人的な電話番号とみられる番号をSNSで一般公開した。

**どこが笑える？**

トランプ大統領、サマータイムを永久化する法案を共和党のコットン上院議員に支持させようとしました。説得が難しかったのか、コットン議員の個人番号らしきものをSNSに投稿して「みんな電話してあげて」と呼びかけました。現職大統領が自党の議員に、8000万人のフォロワーを使って電話攻勢をかける。時計の針をどう動かすかの話が、外交の話になってきた。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 自党の上院議員を説得できない？ 8000万人に番号を投げればいい。党内の根回しって、そういうことでしたっけ。

---

## 4. OpenAI Safety Employee Quits, Publishes Warning — As OpenAI Releases More AI

*The Verge（[記事](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1004408/openai-safety-quits-sounding-the-alarm)）*

OpenAIで主要モデルのリリースごとに安全性レポートを執筆していたデイビッド・ロビンソン氏が同社を退職し、AIの安全性への懸念を公開書簡で表明した。同氏は雑誌「ジ・アトランティック」への寄稿で警鐘を鳴らしており、OpenAIでは安全担当者の退職が相次いでいる。

**どこが笑える？**

OpenAIで主要モデルのリリースごとに「このAIは安全です」という内容のレポートを書いてきたデイビッド・ロビンソン氏が退職し、「実は心配があります」という文章を公開しました。「安全です」という言葉に名前を貸してきた人が、「やはり心配です」と言って出ていく。次のレポートは誰が書くんだろう。まだ辞めてない人が書くんですよね、たぶん。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 「このAIは安全です」と書いてた人が「やっぱりそうじゃないかも」と書いて辞めた。

---

## 5. Pentagon Gets an 'Office of Religious Affairs' Under Hegseth, Who Famously Dislikes 'Weirdos'

*The Guardian US（[記事](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/oct/03/pete-hegseth-office-of-religious-affairs)）*

ピート・ヘグセス国防長官が国防総省に「宗教問題局」を新設すると発表した。ヘグセス長官は「あごひげを生やした者、変人、弱虫は不要」などの発言で知られており、今回の動きは国防総省のキャラクターに関する議論を呼んでいる。

**どこが笑える？**

「あごひげを生やした者、変人、弱虫は軍に不要」と発言したヘグセス国防長官が、国防総省に「宗教問題局」を新設しました。宗教と、あごひげ。この2つが歴史の中でどれだけ深く結びついているか、調べてから発表してほしかったな。政教分離が建前のはずのアメリカで、国防総省が宗教の専門部署を持つ。ペンタゴンの組織図、なかなかのことになっています。

**このニュースをジョークにするなら...**

> 変人はお断り。宗教を扱う局は大歓迎。

---

## 今日のまとめジョーク/パンチライン

> 「安全担当者」という肩書の人が次々に辞めていく職場、ちょっと待って、それどこの話ですかって聞いたら、全部違う会社でした。

今日も読んでくれてありがとうございます。また明日の朝、ここで。
